title: Choose Orifude's new visual world
question: The current site keeps its product truth and brand palette, but loses the border-heavy interface styling. Choose the printed world that should carry the exchange.

options.label: Woodland broadside
options.lineage: relief-printed folktale broadsides and independent press posters
options.thesis: One bold printed sheet makes a private letter feel like an event worth releasing.
options.viewport: An oversized human sentence fills most of the first screen; the squirrel courier and one dark download block complete the composition without cards or framing.
options.risk: The print character must stay contemporary and legible rather than becoming rustic decoration.

raised.raise: One meaningful transition records the moment a letter leaves, while the rest of the page stays still.
The journey is edited down to three unmistakable beats instead of a long stack of sections.
Downloads use whole, confident color fields rather than bordered package cards.

options.label: Literary Sunday edition
options.lineage: independent literary reviews and large-format newspaper features
options.thesis: Orifude reads as a beautifully edited story whose final paragraph is the download.
options.viewport: A generous two-part editorial opening pairs a large promise with the real terminal recording, then moves through a short, readable story.
options.risk: It is the most familiar direction and could feel like a magazine template if the composition becomes polite.

options.label: Cutting-bench sequence
options.lineage: film workprints and physical editing benches
options.thesis: The exchange is cut into a rail of release, carry, and reply frames.
options.viewport: A horizontal three-frame journey leads directly to the working terminal proof.
options.case: The sequence is clear, but the industrial control language does not identify with a private, gentle correspondence ritual.
options.kept: A strict three-beat edit replaces repetitive explanatory sections.
options.risk: Perforations, rails, and labels would recreate the thin-line and monospace clutter the redesign must remove.

options.label: Fold sequence
options.thesis: A single sheet changes state as the visitor learns the exchange.
options.viewport: One sheet folds from message to released letter across the opening.
options.case: The mechanism is immediately clear, but an explicit Japanese craft system conflicts with the requirement not to imply cultural authenticity for a coined name.
options.kept: Each product state stays distinct and recoverable.
options.risk: Literal folding would overwhelm the actual one-to-one correspondence promise.

options.label: Three-ink kiosk
options.lineage: restricted-ink public ephemera and package labels
options.thesis: Each platform release is a strongly printed object in one shared system.
options.viewport: A compact product statement sits above whole-field platform packages.
options.case: It makes distribution strong, but turns the emotional exchange into a package catalog.
options.kept: Whole color fields give downloads enough visual authority without bordered cards.
options.risk: A repeated cell grid would feel like another component library.

outcome: Superseded by direct user feedback. The shipped direction returns to the simpler folded-letter composition recorded in .impeccable/mocks/folded-branch-approved.png, without the page-wide branch, oversized slogan treatment, or overlapping proof.

canonCard.label: Polished product landing page
canonCard.thesis: A conventional product page explains, demonstrates, and distributes Orifude with excellent restraint.
canonCard.viewport: A concise headline, a direct download action, and a polished terminal screenshot follow the expected landing-page hierarchy.
canonCard.risk: It would be easy to use, but intentionally less ownable and memorable.
